key_insight: Combined computational and neural-network modelling identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects, thermal gradients and axial-force fluctuations in HDPE joints.
method: Simulate temperatures, forces, material flow and defects using a three-dimensional Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Combine predictions into process maps distinguishing defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good agreement with CEL predictions; ANN R² values ranged from 0.91 to 0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive performance beyond the tested welding parameters and experimental setup remains unestablished.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
